main_text.p: 226.) quod ita (decretum) ante cæli terræq; (fabricam.) Postea vero devastabitur Domus: & hoc ipsum est (quod dicitur:) Et terra erat inanis & vacua. Et tenebræ, quæ venerunt, obscurârunt mundum, postquam recessit Numinis præsentia. Sed Spiritus Dei, qui requievit, est ille Spiritus sapientiæ & intellectûs, (qui fuit, incubavit) super interpretes legis, quæ assimilatur aquis. Et tandem (dixit): Fiat lux, in diebus Messiæ, Tunc distinguet Deus inter collectionem salutis suæ (salvando-rum suorum,) & inter eos, qui perseverant in caligine operum suorum. Hoc jam Messias noster præstitit, & clarius in novissimo die præstabit. Vid. Galat. de Arcan. Cath. ver. l. 5. c. 10. p. 310. Schickard. Bech. Hap. p. 149. At quis de unica hac voce בראשית Apinas & Tricas Rabbinicas perfectè perlustraret? Et ne plura addam, R. Simhon ben Johai composuit librum suum Ticunin, de 72. combinationibus hujus dictionis, verba sunt Menasis Ben-Isr. l. c. p. 171.
main_text.head: XVIII.
main_text.p: Quidam ראשי תיבות, initiales literas, totius versus observant. De qua observatione Aben Esr. in Præf. cit. וחשבון ראשי מלות פסוק בראשית כנגד כל האותיות Computus initialium literarum respondet omnibus literis. Scilicet literæ capitales sunt: [illegible, ~8 letters] & quia singulæ numerales sunt, conficiunt 22. quot literæ in Hebræorum Alphabetho numerantur. Εὕρημα acumine Rabbinico dignum! Quare non potius 22. librorum, quos Hebræi in V.T. numerant, mentionem faciunt?

XIX. Huic aliam Kabbalæ speciem opponunt, quam סופי תיבות, fines dictionum, appellant, quæ circa Literas vocum finales versatur. Juxta hanc quoque versum Geneseos primum examinant. Ita namque [?] בעל המוריים ludit: בראשית ברא אלהים סופי תיבות אמת מלמד שברא העולם באמת כמו שנאמר ראש דרך אמת ברא אלהים את סופי תיבו׳ אמת וירא אלהים את סופי תיבות אמת ויברא אלהים את סת אמת. וירא אלהים את סת אמת. ברא אלהים לעשות סת אמת לכך תקנו ו׳ פעמים אמת וכו׳ Hoc est: Finales literæ vocum Hebræarum, In principio creavit

page.notes: The top-left "226.)" is read as the printed page number, with the text continuing from the previous page. The line-initial "226.)" may instead be a fragment reference; the first paragraph is marked cont="true" for that reason. Page-number placement and the italic/roman split in parentheses are judgements from a small scan. The sequence after "sunt:" is illegible at this resolution. The Greek "Εὕρημα" is uncertain in its accents. The Hebrew word after "namque" is uncertain: it shows a boxed glyph. The Hebrew block is printed in four lines and was joined into one paragraph here. The "5." in "l. 5. c. 10." is doubtful and may be a long s. The verse Hebrew is hard to read letter by letter and may contain printing errors. The page is set in roman and italic type, not black letter.
